scientificTheAlmanac.name: The Almanac
scientificTheAlmanac.flavor: A year is a book; we learned to read ahead.
scientificTheAlmanac.text: Libraries cost 25% less production and give +1 production.

scientificTheScribesHall.name: The Scribes' Hall
scientificTheScribesHall.flavor: Every hand that can write is a hand that can teach.
scientificTheScribesHall.text: Cities with a Library gain +1 science per four citizens and +1 culture per three citizens.

theCelestialRites.name: The Celestial Rites
theCelestialRites.flavor: The sky keeps its own calendar, and we copied it.
deferred: your capital gathers faith from the sky, and being the first to set eyes on each new kind of country or ground pays faith besides
theCelestialRites.note: Cut from the deck. It paid faith, which is another deck's currency, and its other half repeated another card.

fieldNotebooks.name: Field Notebooks
fieldNotebooks.flavor: Nothing is found twice unless it is written down.
fieldNotebooks.text: Claiming a ruin grants 15 science, 20 culture and 20 gold.
fieldNotebooks.note: Cut from the deck. Exploring belongs to another deck, and this card served none of this deck's themes.

naturalPhilosophy.name: Natural Philosophy
naturalPhilosophy.flavor: Name the world and it begins to answer.
deferred: being the first to set eyes on each new kind of country or ground pays science, and feeds your capital
naturalPhilosophy.note: Cut from the deck. Paying for the first sight of new ground is exploring, which belongs to another deck.

apprenticeEngineers.name: Apprentice Engineers
apprenticeEngineers.flavor: First the book, then the shovel, then the road.
deferred: towns with a library raise workers faster, and the first works of each kind you build on ground of your own pay the town that holds them
apprenticeEngineers.note: Cut from the deck. Its science on mines was a small flat bonus, and faster workers belong to another deck.

theLongStudy.name: The Long Study
theLongStudy.flavor: A roof, a lamp, and a long patience.
theLongStudy.text: A Library at least twenty turns old grants +2 culture and +1 renown. At forty turns, these bonuses become +4 culture and +2 renown.

theResearchAnnals.name: The Research Annals
theResearchAnnals.flavor: Knowledge kept is knowledge that keeps.
deferred: while this sits in council, your capital works and sings for every technology you have completed, up to a limit
theResearchAnnals.note: Cut from the deck. Its words never settled what it paid.

practicalAstronomy.name: Practical Astronomy
practicalAstronomy.flavor: The same stars that steer a ship will feed a town.
practicalAstronomy.text: Scouts and ships gain +1 sight. Coastal cities with a Library gain +3 food.
practicalAstronomy.note: Cut from the deck. Once its sight went to another deck, food in coastal towns with a library served none of this deck's themes.

patientResearch.name: Patient Research
deferred: science buildings cost more to raise, and each one that has stood a long while feeds and works the town it stands in
patientResearch.note: Cut from the deck. It repeated two other cards that pay for old buildings.

theGlassmakersCharter.name: The Glassmakers' Charter
theGlassmakersCharter.flavor: Sand, fire, and a second look at everything.
theGlassmakersCharter.text: Drafting this opens Optics for research. Knowing it lets you build the Specularium, a city building only you can build: +3 food, and +1 science for every two citizens of its town. No chair required.

theOpenCollegium.name: The Open Collegium
theOpenCollegium.flavor: The chair stays empty until the right mind sits in it.
deferred: you gain more renown while no great person of yours is waiting to be spent
theOpenCollegium.note: Cut from the deck. Renown for every kind of great person belongs to another deck.

workingEstates.name: Working Estates
workingEstates.flavor: A great mind leaves a field behind it.
workingEstates.text: Worked great-person improvements gain +5 food and +3 gold.
workingEstates.note: Cut from the deck. It paid on every great person's works, and other cards now pay on the academy.

theOldAcademy.name: The Old Academy
theOldAcademy.flavor: Ivy is the proof of teaching.
theOldAcademy.text: An Academy at least twenty turns old gains +3 food and +3 production. At forty turns these bonuses become +6 of each.

learnedCommissions.name: Learned Commissions
learnedCommissions.flavor: Commission the hall before you commission the statue.
learnedCommissions.text: Library cities gain +38% production toward empire buildings. Completing each institution type for the first time grants 60 culture and 30 faith.

theStrategicReserves.name: The School of Mines
theStrategicReserves.flavor: Teach the assayer on the hill, and the hill pays the fees.
theStrategicReserves.text: An Academy standing on a strategic resource supplies one more copy of it.

thePracticalArts.name: The Practical Arts
thePracticalArts.flavor: Study what you are already doing, and do it better.
deferred: technologies that match what your empire already does cost less to research, while ordinary soldiers cost more to raise
thePracticalArts.note: Cut from the deck. It made ordinary research cheaper, and this deck spends its science on charters.

researchThroughConstruction.name: Research through Construction
researchThroughConstruction.flavor: We learned the arch by raising it.
deferred: your towns' science becomes production instead, and finishing an ordinary building pays research worth part of its price
researchThroughConstruction.note: Cut from the deck. It turned science into production, and it had too many parts.

theEndowedProvinces.name: The Endowed Provinces
theEndowedProvinces.flavor: A gift of learning keeps giving grain.
theEndowedProvinces.text: Each city working at least one great-person improvement gains +6 food and +5 production, once per city.
theEndowedProvinces.note: Cut from the deck. Another card already pays food and production for an old academy.

theMetallurgistsCharter.name: The Metallurgists' Charter
deferred: drafting this opens the study of alloys for research
theMetallurgistsCharter.note: Cut from the deck. Its gift needed a new kind of soldier, and other charters now improve the land army instead.

theNaturalistsCharter.name: The Naturalists' Charter
theNaturalistsCharter.flavor: Give the beast a name and the field a page.
deferred: drafting this opens the study of living things for research
theNaturalistsCharter.note: Cut from the deck. It was a plain bonus to farmland behind a charter, the weakest of them.

theRoyalSociety.name: The Royal Society
theRoyalSociety.flavor: Letters after a name, and lamps in every window.
theRoyalSociety.text: Each empire building grants +2 renown. Its city gains +2 happiness, once per city.
theRoyalSociety.note: Cut from the deck. Its happiness repeated another card, and renown for every kind of great person belongs to another deck.

theLearnedChancery.name: The Learned Chancery
theLearnedChancery.flavor: The clerk with a book governs further than the clerk with a seal.
theLearnedChancery.text: Cities with an empire building cost one less authority, minimum one, and gain +50% border growth.
theLearnedChancery.note: Cut from the deck. Cheaper towns and faster borders belong to another deck.

theAcademyQuarter.name: The Academy Quarter
theAcademyQuarter.flavor: Put the schools on one street and listen.
theAcademyQuarter.text: A city with an empire building gains +5 production and +5 gold per different great-person work type it works, at most +25 of each. Multiple institutions do not multiply this benefit.
theAcademyQuarter.note: Cut from the deck. It was one card too many paying on academies.

theInheritedSchool.name: The Inherited School
theInheritedSchool.flavor: The teacher dies; the lesson keeps its chair.
deferred: worked academies and manufactories feed and work the better for each different family of great person whose legacy you still keep, up to a limit
theInheritedSchool.note: Cut from the deck. Counting the kinds of great person belongs to another deck.

discoveriesThroughGreatPeople.name: Discoveries through Great People
discoveriesThroughGreatPeople.flavor: A life spent well is a chapter finished early.
deferred: spending a great person on an act, a work or a legacy pays part of the research you are studying, at most once in a turn
discoveriesThroughGreatPeople.note: Cut from the deck. Other cards pay for a great scholar's moment.

husbandryStudies.name: Husbandry Studies
husbandryStudies.flavor: Study the horse and the horse goes further.
deferred: soldiers of yours that depend on horses are quicker on their feet from the day they are raised, and stay so
husbandryStudies.note: Cut from the deck. Faster horsemen belong to another deck, and the gain was small.

enduringInstitutions.name: Enduring Institutions
enduringInstitutions.flavor: What is old enough to be trusted is old enough to be useful.
enduringInstitutions.text: A city with an empire building at least twenty turns old gains +2 happiness and +23% production, once per city.

thePatentRolls.name: The Patent Rolls
thePatentRolls.flavor: First is a fact, and facts are worth recording.
thePatentRolls.text: Completing a technology before any other empire grants 30 culture and 10 renown.
thePatentRolls.note: Cut from the deck. Another card pays for finishing a technology first.

commissionsOfService.name: Commissions of Service
commissionsOfService.flavor: Send the great where the need is, not where the marble is.
deferred: spending a great person on an act or a legacy pays food and gold to your nearest town, though placing a work does not
commissionsOfService.note: Cut from the deck. Paying for spending any great person belongs to another deck.

theQuietFaculties.name: The Quiet Faculties
theQuietFaculties.flavor: Quiet halls, full barns, and very few drums.
theQuietFaculties.text: Cities working a great-person improvement gain +38% food and +30% production, but produce military units 25% more slowly.

theMechanistsCharter.name: The Mechanists' Charter
theMechanistsCharter.text: Drafting this opens Mechanics for research. Knowing it gives two lines a trait they keep through every upgrade. Onager (Catapult and Trebuchet): +1 range. Repeating Crossbow (Archer to Crossbowman): it may move after it shoots. No chair required.

theAlchemistsCharter.name: The Alchemists' Charter
theAlchemistsCharter.flavor: Turn one thing into another and call it a trade.
theAlchemistsCharter.text: Drafting this opens Chemistry for research. Knowing it gives the Grenadier trait to the Warrior line (Warrior to Longswordsman), kept through every upgrade: +1 strength, and +1 more for each charter technology you know. Workers may build Niter Beds beside a farm or pasture, which supply one niter. Chemistry does not open the Magnum Opus. No chair required.

theSecondSeat.name: The Second Seat
theSecondSeat.flavor: One of a kind is a habit, not a law.
deferred: you may raise one further copy of an empire building, in a town that holds a university, and only one such copy may be building or standing at a time

theLongInheritance.name: The Long Inheritance
theLongInheritance.flavor: Old works build the new ones.
theLongInheritance.text: Cities working an Academy at least twenty turns old gain +30% production toward empire buildings, wonders and the Magnum Opus.

masterArtificers.name: Master Artificers
masterArtificers.flavor: The hands that made the tools now make everything else.
masterArtificers.text: Worked Academies and Manufactories gain +9 production and +9 gold.
masterArtificers.note: Cut from the deck. Another card already pays production on an academy.

theDistantColleges.name: The Distant Colleges
theDistantColleges.flavor: Learning travels further than a cart.
deferred: a town holding an empire building may work your great people's works one hex beyond its usual reach, and gains no ground and no citizens by it
theDistantColleges.note: Cut from the deck. It needed a new rule that no other card used.

theSocietyOfArtificers.name: The Society of Artificers
theSocietyOfArtificers.flavor: Bread and song out of a workshop.
theSocietyOfArtificers.text: A city with an empire building working an Academy or Manufactory gains food and culture each equal to 30% of its base production, excluding conversion outputs.
theSocietyOfArtificers.note: Cut from the deck. It stacked three conditions to say one thing.

theLearnedRealm.name: The Learned Realm
theLearnedRealm.flavor: A realm that reads is a realm that holds together.
theLearnedRealm.text: Each city working a great-person improvement grants +1 authority capacity, at most +8. Cities with a Library at least twenty turns old gain +2 happiness.
theLearnedRealm.note: Cut from the deck. Authority belongs to another deck, and its two halves had nothing to do with each other.

theHerbalistsCharter.name: The Herbalists' Charter
theHerbalistsCharter.flavor: A walled garden, and a book for every bed in it.
theHerbalistsCharter.text: Drafting this opens Herbals for research. Knowing it lets workers build the Physic Garden on flat land with fresh water, one in each town: +2 science and +2 happiness. No chair required.

theBronzeFoundersCharter.name: The Bronze-Founders' Charter
theBronzeFoundersCharter.flavor: The guild keeps the mould, and the city keeps the guild.
theBronzeFoundersCharter.text: Drafting this opens Casting for research. Knowing it gives two lines a trait they keep through every upgrade. Hoplite (Spearman to Pikeman): +1 strength, and in one of your towns +1 more for every four citizens there. Maryannu (War Chariot to Knight): +1 strength, and +5 against a unit below half health. No chair required.

theSurveyorsCharter.name: The Surveyors' Charter
theSurveyorsCharter.flavor: Chain, rod and level, and the land agrees to be measured.
theSurveyorsCharter.text: Drafting this opens Surveying for research. Knowing it lets you build the Aqueduct before Engineering, and lets workers build the Qanat: an improvement on flat land that waters the farms beside it with no river or lake nearby. No chair required.

theLibrariansCharter.name: The Librarians' Charter
theLibrariansCharter.flavor: A shelf in order is a city in order.
theLibrariansCharter.text: Drafting this opens Cataloguing for research. Knowing it lets you build the Mouseion, an empire building only you can build: +4 renown a turn, favouring great scholars, and +2 culture for each empire building you hold, itself included. It costs 30% more production than an ordinary empire building. No chair required.

theCommonplaceBook.name: The Commonplace Book
theCommonplaceBook.flavor: Copy out what you read, and you read it twice.
theCommonplaceBook.text: Charter technologies cost you 15% less research.

thePaperMakersCharter.name: The Paper-Makers' Charter
thePaperMakersCharter.flavor: The mill by the river turns rags into records.
thePaperMakersCharter.text: Drafting this opens Papermaking for research. Knowing it lets you build the Scriptorium: +2 science, and +10% science in a town with an Academy in its borders. No chair required.

thePhysiciansCharter.name: The Physicians' Charter
thePhysiciansCharter.flavor: A house of healing, open to every traveller.
thePhysiciansCharter.text: Drafting this opens Medicine for research. Knowing it lets you build the Bimaristan, an empire building: +25% food in its town, and your units heal 10 more a turn in your land. No chair required.

thePrintersCharter.name: The Printers' Charter
thePrintersCharter.flavor: Small books, carried in a merchant's pocket.
thePrintersCharter.text: Drafting this opens Printing for research. Knowing it lets you build the Aldine Press, a city building only you can build: +2 culture, and trade routes from its town gain +2 science and +2 culture. It also gives +1 trade route. No chair required.

theGunfoundersCharter.name: The Gunfounders' Charter
theGunfoundersCharter.flavor: The foundry by the arsenal never lets its fires go out.
theGunfoundersCharter.text: Drafting this opens Gunfounding for research. Knowing it lets you build the Tophane, an empire building: military units gained in its town start with +4 strength, and it builds them 25% faster. No chair required.

theMilitaryEngineersCharter.name: The Military Engineers' Charter
theMilitaryEngineersCharter.flavor: The engineers draw the walls before the masons lay them.
theMilitaryEngineersCharter.text: Drafting this opens Military Architecture for research. Knowing it lets you build the Bastion (+5 defence, +30 hit points), which no ordinary technology opens. No chair required.

theNavalGunnersCharter.name: The Naval Gunners' Charter
theNavalGunnersCharter.flavor: Oars for the calm, and guns for the battle.
theNavalGunnersCharter.text: Drafting this opens Naval Gunnery for research. Knowing it gives your Gun Galleys the Galleass trait: +3 strength, and they blockade: parked off a rival's port, a Gun Galley closes its sea lane and its trade. No chair required.

thePatentOffice.name: The Patent Office
thePatentOffice.flavor: Register the invention, and the next one costs less to argue for.
thePatentOffice.text: Charter technologies cost you no more research than ordinary technologies at the same point in the tree.

theScholarsGuild.name: The Scholars' Guild
theScholarsGuild.flavor: The guild feeds its students and mends their tools, and asks for lessons in return.
theScholarsGuild.text: Scholars in the trades also pay +1 food and +1 production.

theSecretArts.name: The Secret Arts
theSecretArts.flavor: What the workshop knows, the workshop keeps.
theSecretArts.text: Each town gains +1 production for each technology you know that no empire you have met knows, at most +5.

theEdgeOfTheSword.name: The Edge of the Sword
theEdgeOfTheSword.flavor: Better steel ends the argument sooner.
theEdgeOfTheSword.text: Your units gain +3 strength against the units of an empire that knows fewer technologies than you.

theTranslationMovement.name: The Translation Movement
theTranslationMovement.flavor: It is quicker to translate a book than to write it again.
theTranslationMovement.text: Technologies that an empire you have met already knows cost you 20% less research.

theGreatDesigns.name: The Great Designs
theGreatDesigns.flavor: Raise it before anyone else knows how.
theGreatDesigns.text: Your towns build a wonder 30% faster while no empire you have met knows the technology that opens it.

greekFire.name: Greek Fire
greekFire.flavor: The recipe was a secret of the state, and it stayed one.
greekFire.text: Gaining a unit that no empire you have met can build grants science and culture equal to its strength.

theProvingGround.name: The Proving Ground
theProvingGround.flavor: Every new idea is tried in the field before it is trusted.
theProvingGround.text: Your units gain +1 strength for each technology you know that no empire you have met knows, at most +8.

theProspectorsNotes.name: The Prospectors' Notes
theProspectorsNotes.flavor: Mark where the rock changes colour, and dig there first.
theProspectorsNotes.text: Building a mine or a quarry grants its town 25 production.

theFoundingGift.name: The Founding Gift
theFoundingGift.flavor: The scholar brings the books, and the town brings the stone.
theFoundingGift.text: A great scholar who founds an Academy also grants its town 150 production.

theLatinQuarter.name: The Latin Quarter
theLatinQuarter.flavor: The students speak one tongue, and the streets learn it.
theLatinQuarter.text: Great-person works beside an Academy gain +2 culture and +1 production.

theStudiumGenerale.name: The Studium Generale
theStudiumGenerale.flavor: Any hall where masters teach is a school of the whole world.
theStudiumGenerale.text: Great-person works beside an Academy count as Academies for your cards.

theNizamiyya.name: The Nizamiyya
theNizamiyya.flavor: Endow the chair, and the chair outlives the vizier.
theNizamiyya.text: Academies produce half again of everything they make.

theRepublicOfLetters.name: The Republic of Letters
theRepublicOfLetters.flavor: No borders but the margins, and every scholar a citizen.
theRepublicOfLetters.text: Your capital gains +4 production and +4 culture for each Academy you hold.

theRoyalWorkshops.name: The Royal Workshops
theRoyalWorkshops.flavor: Each new idea goes first to the workshops behind the palace.
theRoyalWorkshops.text: Completing a technology grants 15 production in your capital.

thePrizeEssay.name: The Prize Essay
thePrizeEssay.flavor: The academy sets the question, and the whole country tries to answer it first.
thePrizeEssay.text: Completing a technology before any other empire grants 15 culture and 15 production in your capital. Charter technologies do not count.

theSkyWatchers.name: The Sky Watchers
theSkyWatchers.flavor: The priests kept the calendar, so the priests watched the sky.

theAstronomicalDiaries.name: The Astronomical Diaries
theAstronomicalDiaries.flavor: Every night is written down, and the book is never finished.
theAstronomicalDiaries.text: While seated, this card gains +1 culture and +1 production each time you complete a technology. It starts at +2 of each.

theScholarsFame.name: The Scholars' Fame
theScholarsFame.flavor: A hard problem solved makes a name, and a name draws students.
theScholarsFame.text: Completing a technology grants renown, favouring great scholars, equal to a twentieth of its cost.

theCharterRolls.name: The Charter Rolls
theCharterRolls.flavor: Each charter is copied into the rolls, and each copy brings a fee.
theCharterRolls.text: Your capital gains +3 production and +3 culture for each charter you have drafted.

theRoyalCharterCommission.name: The Royal Charter Commission
theRoyalCharterCommission.flavor: The crown pays for the first result, and the scholars know it.
theRoyalCharterCommission.text: Commission. Complete a charter technology while this is seated. Reward: a great scholar and 100 culture. Then it leaves its chair.

theAgeOfReason.name: The Age of Reason
theAgeOfReason.flavor: Each discovery is worth two, because it teaches how to make the next.
theAgeOfReason.text: Your Orders count each technology you complete twice.

theJourneymen.name: The Journeymen
theJourneymen.flavor: The new method walks from town to town with the men who learned it.
theJourneymen.text: Completing a technology grants each town production equal to three times its population.

theSumOfKnowledge.name: The Sum of Knowledge
theSumOfKnowledge.flavor: Everything we know, in one place, in order.
theSumOfKnowledge.text: Your capital gains +1 production and +1 culture for each technology you know.

theGreatCatalogue.name: The Great Catalogue
theGreatCatalogue.flavor: Every chartered art has its page, and the last page is the Great Work.
theGreatCatalogue.text: +10% production toward the Magnum Opus for each charter technology you know, at most +40%.
